submission.justification:
Crystal-K3 at 5 cm thickness is recommended as the optimal choice for the gamma spectrometer scintillator stage. 

Among the three candidates, Crystal-K1 fails the hard background constraint with 2.0 counts/kg/day, which is 4× the allowed budget of 0.5 counts/kg/day. This leaves Crystal-K2 and Crystal-K3 as viable options.

While both K2 and K3 meet the background requirement, they differ significantly in energy resolution performance:
- Crystal-K2 achieves best resolution of 8.33% at 5 cm thickness
- Crystal-K3 achieves best resolution of 4.487% at 5 cm thickness

Crystal-K3 provides approximately 46% better energy resolution than K2, which is critical for the facility's assay programme at 662 keV. The superior resolution will enable better discrimination of gamma-ray peaks and more accurate material screening for the dark-matter experiment.

The optimization study across thicknesses from 2-10 cm confirmed that 5 cm is optimal for K3, providing the best balance for 662 keV gamma detection. At this thickness, K3 maintains a comfortable safety margin on the background budget (0.3 vs 0.5 counts/kg/day limit) while delivering exceptional energy resolution.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 at 5 cm achieves 4.487% resolution at 662 keV, which is the best among all viable options. K2's best resolution is 8.33%, making K3 approximately 46% better.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates listed
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 is one of the three candidate crystals (K1, K2, K3) specified in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Intrinsic background must not exceed 0.5 counts/kg/day (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 has background of 0.3 counts/kg/day, which is below the 0.5 counts/kg/day budget. Crystal-K1 fails this constraint with 2.0 counts/kg/day.
Recommended thickness of 5 cm falls within the specified range of 2-10 cm.
